source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-271065:Diagonal player movement is not normalized when holding two movement keys
source_meta._title: Player movement at low speeds is biased towards cardinal directions

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 in a single-player Creative-mode Superflat world with commands/cheats enabled. Use the default Classic Flat preset so the grass surface is at Y=3 and the player's standing Y coordinate is 4. Default controls are referenced: W for Forward, Left Shift for Sneak, T for chat, F3 for the debug overlay, and right-click for block interaction.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, not fix version 25w02a or a later version.
Use an unmodified vanilla client. Disable mods, movement-altering clients, and datapacks that alter player attributes or movement.
Create a single-player world with Game Mode set to Creative, Allow Cheats set to ON, and World Type set to Superflat using the default Classic Flat preset.
Use one player only so the @a trail command and @p teleport command operate on the intended player.
Use default Forward and Sneak bindings, or identify the rebound keys that perform those actions.

During each measured movement pass, do not press A, S, D, jump, sprint, or provide mouse/controller look input. Camera adjustment is permitted only after movement has stopped so the lever can be switched.
Do not remove the armor stands after the first pass; both trails must remain for the later observation handoff.

steps.action: From the Minecraft Launcher, start a clean installation of Java Edition 1.15.2 and wait for the main menu to load.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left portion of the main menu identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.15.2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, and cycle World Type to Superflat. Leave the default Classic Flat preset selected, then create the world.
steps.success_cue: The player appears in Creative mode on a level grass plane extending beyond the visible area.

steps.action: Wait until the nearby terrain is fully rendered and normal movement and input respond without world-loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding flat-world chunks are visible and player movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the build-position teleport command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the flat grass near X=0, Y=4, Z=3.5 and is looking generally north toward decreasing Z.

steps.action: Open chat, execute the setblock command to place the Impulse command block at X=0, Y=4, Z=0, and close chat after execution.
steps.success_cue: A normal orange Impulse command block is visible on top of the grass at X=0, Y=4, Z=0.

steps.action: Open chat and execute the setblock command to place the Repeating command block immediately north of the Impulse command block, at X=0, Y=4, Z=-1.
steps.success_cue: A purple Repeating command block is directly adjacent to the north side of the orange Impulse command block.

steps.action: Right-click the purple Repeating command block at X=0, Y=4, Z=-1. In its configuration screen, ensure the mode reads Repeat, the condition reads Unconditional, and the redstone setting reads Needs Redstone. Enter the report-supplied armor-stand command in the Console Command field and select Done. Retain the supplied leading slash if the UI accepts it; if the UI automatically removes only that slash, leave all remaining command text unchanged.
steps.success_cue: The purple command block is configured as Repeat, Unconditional, Needs Redstone, with the supplied summon command stored in it.

steps.action: Right-click the orange Impulse command block at X=0, Y=4, Z=0. Ensure its mode reads Impulse, its condition reads Unconditional, and its redstone setting reads Needs Redstone. Enter the deterministic teleport command and select Done. The target is approximately ten blocks south of the lever; yaw 174 is six degrees away from the nearest cardinal yaw of 180, and pitch 0 keeps the view level.
steps.success_cue: The orange command block is configured as Impulse, Unconditional, Needs Redstone, with the teleport command stored in it.

steps.action: Press T, enter the give command including the leading slash, and press Enter to obtain one lever.
steps.success_cue: A Lever is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Lever by scrolling to it or pressing the corresponding number key. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the screen; the selected slot has a highlighted outline.
steps.success_cue: The lever is shown in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Stand on the south side of the orange Impulse command block—the open side facing positive Z and opposite the purple Repeating command block. Aim at the orange block's south vertical face and right-click once to attach the lever directly to that face. Do not switch it on yet.
steps.success_cue: An unpowered lever is attached to the south face of the orange command block, with the purple command block still directly behind the orange block to the north.

steps.action: Press F3 to display the debug overlay and leave it visible during both movement passes so the player's coordinates can be used as a stopping reference.
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay displays the player's XYZ coordinates and facing information.

steps.action: Move to the south side of the attached lever, close enough to interact with it. Aim the crosshair directly at the lever until its selection outline is visible. After establishing this aim, stop providing mouse or other look-direction input.
steps.success_cue: The lever is under the crosshair and can be activated with right-click without moving the camera.

steps.action: Right-click the lever once. This powers both adjacent command blocks: the Impulse command block teleports the player to the prepared starting position, and the Repeating command block begins summoning small armor stands at the player's successive positions.
steps.success_cue: The view jumps to approximately X=1.55, Y=4, Z=11.5 with yaw 174, and small armor stands begin appearing at or behind the player.

steps.action: As soon as the teleport has completed and movement responds, press and continuously hold only Forward, normally W. Do not sneak, sprint, jump, strafe, or provide look input during this first pass.
steps.success_cue: The player is walking forward across the flat ground while facing the command-block setup, and the powered Repeating command block is leaving an armor-stand trail.

steps.action: Continue holding W until the player is close to the lever. Use the debug Z coordinate as a deterministic reference and release W when Z is approximately 3.5, before colliding with the command block. Do not adjust the camera until W has been released.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary about two blocks south of the lever, and the first armor-stand trail extends from the teleport location toward the command blocks.

steps.action: After the player is fully stationary, camera movement no longer affects the recorded movement path. Re-aim at the lever if necessary and right-click it once to turn it off.
steps.success_cue: The lever is in its unpowered position, the player remains near the command blocks, and the Repeating command block is no longer adding armor stands to the trail.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the now-unpowered lever again until it can be activated. Once aimed, stop providing look input in preparation for the sneaking pass.
steps.success_cue: The unpowered lever is targeted by the crosshair and can be activated without changing the camera direction.

steps.action: Right-click the lever once to power the command blocks for the second pass. Allow the Impulse command block to teleport the player back to the same start position and orientation.
steps.success_cue: The player is again at approximately X=1.55, Y=4, Z=11.5 with yaw 174, and the Repeating command block has resumed summoning armor stands.

steps.action: Press and hold the Sneak action, which is Left Shift by default. Keep it held without pressing a movement key yet.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the sneaking state at the teleport position and has not started the second movement path.

steps.action: While continuing to hold Sneak, press and continuously hold Forward, normally W. Keep both inputs held. Do not press A, S, D, sprint, jump, or provide look input while moving.
steps.success_cue: The player is moving forward slowly in the sneaking state while the Repeating command block records the route with small armor stands.

steps.action: Continue holding both W and Left Shift until the player is close to the lever. Release W when the debug Z coordinate is approximately 3.5, before colliding with the command-block setup. Keep the camera unchanged until forward movement has stopped.
steps.success_cue: Forward movement has stopped near the lever, and the second armor-stand trail has been recorded from the same teleport position.

steps.action: Release Left Shift after W has been released so the player stops sneaking without adding further forward movement.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary near the command blocks and is no longer sneaking.

steps.action: After all movement keys are released, re-aim at the lever if necessary and right-click it once to turn off the command blocks.
steps.success_cue: The lever is unpowered, armor stands are no longer being summoned, and both completed armor-stand movement trails remain on the flat plane.

steps.action: Do not move the player through either trail, operate the lever again, remove armor stands, or alter the command blocks. Leave the world in this completed state for the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary beside the unpowered lever, and the normal-speed and sneaking movement paths are both preserved as armor-stand trails.

stor.handoff_condition: The second, sneaking movement pass has been completed; W and Left Shift have been released; the lever and both command blocks are unpowered; and the two armor-stand trails remain in place. Begin observation without moving the player or changing the trails.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a world seed, exact build coordinates, exact starting coordinates, or an exact pitch value. The plan uses the default Classic Flat world and a deterministic setup at X=0, Y=4, Z=0, with a teleport target of X=1.55, Y=4, Z=11.5, yaw 174, and pitch 0. These values satisfy the report's requirement for a position about ten blocks away and a yaw six degrees away from a cardinal direction.

The report does not require a specific game mode or server type. Single-player Creative mode with cheats enabled was selected as the simplest deterministic way to configure command blocks without altering the movement condition being tested.

The report does not specify which face of which command block should receive the lever. This plan attaches it to the south face of the Impulse command block, with the Repeating command block directly adjacent on the north side, implementing the report's instruction that one lever power the two adjacent command blocks.

The exact teleport command was constructed for this plan rather than copied from the report. Its yaw value of 174 is copied from the report's example, while its coordinates and pitch are practical choices.

The report references W and Shift without stating whether controls were rebound. The plan assumes the default W and Left Shift bindings; equivalent rebound Forward and Sneak controls should be used if necessary.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition. Execute the report's exact wither-rose reproduction in affected release 1.16.5 using an unmodified vanilla client and a single-player world (integrated server). Use Creative mode with cheats for setup, then Survival mode for the trigger. Use Normal difficulty and default keyboard/mouse controls or their rebound equivalents. The recommended_version field remains the first listed affected version as required, but the supplied modern reproduction is not executable unchanged in Minecraft 1.6.1.
preconditions: Create a new disposable world rather than opening an important existing world.
Do not install mods, including Physics Mod, because the report's reproduction concerns vanilla client/server state.
Commands must be permitted. In single-player, create the world with Allow Cheats set to ON.
Begin in Creative mode so the wither rose can be placed safely before changing to Survival mode.
Use a new player with no armor, no active status effects, and an otherwise empty inventory and hotbar.
Keep at least two adjacent hotbar slots available: slot 1 for the attribute-modified dirt and slot 2 left empty for deselecting it.
Use a patch of solid grass or dirt with enough open space to approach a single placed wither rose without contacting other hazards.
Do not use the fixed version 1.17 Pre-release 1 or any later version for this reproduction.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for Java Edition 1.16.5, launch it, and wait for the title screen. Do not use a modded launcher profile.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running game as Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.5.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options and set Allow Cheats to ON, then create the world. The seed and world type may remain at their defaults.
steps.success_cue: A new world opens with the player in Creative mode and able to fly.

steps.action: Wait before continuing until nearby terrain has rendered, the player can move normally, and opening chat or inventory responds without initial world-loading delay.
steps.success_cue: Nearby blocks are fully rendered and player controls respond normally.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the difficulty command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that the difficulty has been set to Normal.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, click the search field, type "wither rose", and place one Wither Rose into hotbar slot 9, which is the rightmost slot in the nine-slot bar at the bottom of the screen. Close the inventory with E.
steps.success_cue: A Wither Rose item is visible in hotbar slot 9 and the inventory screen is closed.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 9 by pressing 9. Aim at the top face of a grass block or dirt block in the open test area and use the Place Block action, default right-click, once to place the wither rose.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one planted wither rose is standing on the selected grass or dirt block.

steps.action: Move at least two horizontal blocks away from the planted wither rose. Face the rose and line up a straight, unobstructed walking path to it, but do not touch it yet.
steps.success_cue: The rose remains visible ahead, the player is not occupying its block, and no status-effect icon is present.

steps.action: Press T, enter the game-mode command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The Survival health and hunger bars are visible, and the player can no longer fly indefinitely.

steps.action: While still standing away from the rose, press T, enter the report's item command exactly as shown including the leading slash and all NBT punctuation, and press Enter. Execute it in in-game chat, not a server console.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that dirt was given to the nearest player, and a dirt item is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Press E to open the Survival inventory. Move the newly given dirt item into hotbar slot 1, the leftmost hotbar slot. Remove any item from hotbar slot 2 so that slot 2 is empty. Leave the wither rose item in slot 9 or elsewhere; it must not occupy slot 2. Close the inventory with E.
steps.success_cue: The modified dirt is in hotbar slot 1, hotbar slot 2 is empty, and the inventory screen is closed.

steps.action: Press 1 to make hotbar slot 1 active and hold the attribute-modified dirt in the player's main hand. Do not place or drop the dirt.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 is highlighted, dirt is visible in the player's main hand, and the health capacity has expanded to 40 health points, displayed as 20 heart icons.

steps.action: With the dirt still selected, press T, enter the report's healing command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and all heart icons in the expanded 40-point health bar are filled.

steps.action: Wait only until the Instant Health command has finished applying and normal movement input responds. Keep the dirt selected, remain away from the wither rose, and do not take any damage during this wait.
steps.success_cue: The player remains stationary away from the rose with the modified dirt still selected and the expanded health bar filled.

steps.action: Press 2 to switch the active hotbar selection from the modified dirt in slot 1 to the empty slot 2. Do not select the dirt again, open the inventory, heal again, or take any other damage before entering the rose.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 2 is highlighted, the player's main hand is empty, and the dirt remains stored in slot 1 but is not active.

steps.action: Immediately walk straight into the planted wither rose using the Forward action, default W. Stop moving when the player's feet occupy the same block space as the rose, and remain in contact long enough for the rose's Wither effect to apply. Do not jump, select the dirt, or leave the rose block before the first health update.
steps.exact_input: Hold W until occupying the wither rose, then release W
steps.success_cue: The player's feet overlap the planted wither rose while empty hotbar slot 2 remains active; the observation subsystem must now monitor the resulting health and UI updates.

steps.action: While observation remains active, if the Death Screen interface becomes available, wait only until its controls are interactable and then left-click the Respawn button exactly once. Do not press Escape, disconnect, issue a command, or click Title Screen first. If no Death Screen appears, do not fabricate this action; leave the state unchanged for the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: If the button was presented, exactly one Respawn click has been sent and any immediate UI transition can be observed; otherwise no additional input has altered the triggered state.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just entered and remained inside the planted wither rose while the max-health dirt is deselected and empty hotbar slot 2 is active. Begin observation immediately at this state and keep observation active through the conditional Respawn click described in step 16.
uncertainties: The required recommended_version is the first affected entry, Minecraft 1.6.1, but the report's rewritten primary reproduction uses a wither rose, which was not added to Java Edition until snapshot 18w43a for the 1.14 development cycle. Therefore, the exact supplied path cannot be executed unchanged in Minecraft 1.6.1. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-snapshot-18w43a?utm_source=openai))

The supplied item command uses the snake_case attribute name generic.max_health and an int-array UUID. Attribute names were changed to forms including generic.max_health during the 1.16 development cycle, while pre-1.16 attribute modifiers used UUIDMost and UUIDLeast rather than the int-array UUID form. This is why the plan departs from the first affected version and uses affected release 1.16.5 for the exact primary steps. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Java%E7%89%881.16/%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%91%E7%89%88%E6%9C%AC?variant=zh-tw&utm_source=openai))

The report does not explicitly name which affected version its rewritten wither-rose command sequence targets. Version 1.16.5 is selected as a stable affected release compatible with the report's modern block, command, attribute-name, and UUID era.
No world seed, coordinates, dedicated-server requirement, multiplayer requirement, or special graphics setting is supplied by the report.

Step 16 is necessarily conditional because the Respawn control is only available if the preceding trigger produces the interface described by the report. Whether that interface appears is for the observation subsystem to evaluate, not for this plan to assume.

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 15w41b in a new single-player world, using a keyboard and mouse. Create the world in Creative mode with commands/cheats available, obtain and equip an Elytra, then change to Survival mode while airborne so the normal Survival inventory player-model panel can be opened during an Elytra glide. Use full-screen mode to provide clear far-left and far-right cursor positions. Do not use fix version 25w44a.
preconditions: The launcher must be configured to make historical Java Edition snapshots available and must have a working installation for snapshot 15w41b.
Use an unmodified client without gameplay, rendering, inventory, or player-animation mods. Disable shaders and custom resource packs unless the report is being separately tested for compatibility.
Use a new disposable world; no world seed or coordinates are required by the report.
Use the configured control for Jump, default Space; Inventory, default E; Chat, default T; and Debug Screen, default F3. If controls are rebound, use the actions corresponding to those bindings.
The world must permit commands so that the player can change from Creative mode to Survival mode after obtaining the Elytra and gaining altitude.
Leave the chest armor slot empty before equipping the Elytra.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Java Edition installation for snapshot 15w41b. On the main menu, verify that the displayed version is 15w41b rather than an earlier affected version or fix version 25w44a.
steps.success_cue: The 15w41b main menu is displayed and identifies the running client as snapshot 15w41b.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and ensure commands or cheats are allowed. No particular seed or world type is required. Create the world.
steps.success_cue: A new Creative-mode single-player world begins loading.

steps.action: Wait without performing the test until the terrain around the player has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, chunks are no longer visibly appearing around the spawn area, and the player responds normally to movement input.

steps.action: Switch Minecraft to full-screen mode. Use the Fullscreen control in the video settings if the operating system intercepts the default shortcut.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft window occupies the full display and has distinct far-left and far-right screen edges available for cursor movement.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the Inventory control.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory search tab, select its search field, and search for the Elytra. Left-click the Elytra result and place one Elytra into an empty hotbar slot; the hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the interface.
steps.success_cue: One Elytra is present in a hotbar slot.

steps.action: Open the Survival Inventory section of the Creative inventory—the section containing the player model, crafting grid, main inventory, and four armor slots. Drag the Elytra from the hotbar into the chest armor slot, which is the second armor slot from the top beside the player model.
steps.success_cue: The Elytra icon occupies the chest armor slot and the player is wearing it rather than carrying it only in the hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory and return to first-person world control.
steps.success_cue: The world view is active and the inventory interface is closed.

steps.action: Open the debug screen and rotate horizontally until its facing-direction information says the player is facing south, toward positive Z. This direction is selected because the report comments identify southward Elytra flight as a particularly clear orientation case.
steps.success_cue: The debug screen reports that the player is facing south or toward positive Z.

steps.action: Start Creative flight by double-pressing the Jump control. While flying, hold Jump to ascend. Continue ascending until the debug screen shows a Y coordinate of at least 180, leaving enough height to open and inspect the inventory during the subsequent glide.
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering in Creative flight at Y=180 or higher, with the ground well below.

steps.action: Release Jump while remaining in Creative flight. Reconfirm that the player is facing south, aim slightly downward so forward motion will descend gradually, and then close the debug screen without changing direction.
steps.success_cue: The normal world view is visible, the player is hovering high above the terrain, and the view remains directed generally south with a slight downward pitch.

steps.action: Open in-game chat, type the historical version-compatible game-mode command exactly as shown with the leading slash, and press Enter. Execute it in chat, not in a server console.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports a successful game-mode change, the Survival hearts and hunger HUD are present, and the airborne player begins falling.

steps.action: As soon as the player is descending, press the Jump control once to deploy the equipped Elytra. Aim slightly below the horizon and hold Forward, default W, to establish a southward glide. Do not double-press Jump, because the player is now in Survival mode.
steps.success_cue: The motion changes from a near-vertical fall to sustained forward gliding with a shallower descent, and the player remains well above the ground.

steps.action: While the Elytra glide is still active and before approaching the ground, release movement controls and open the normal Survival inventory using the Inventory control. Opening this interface does not require landing first.
steps.success_cue: The Survival inventory is open, its player-model panel is visible, and the world continues running while the airborne glide state remains active.

steps.action: Move the mouse cursor to the far-left side of the full-screen Minecraft display, keeping it within the game interface. Pause only long enough to establish the cursor position; do not close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: The cursor is positioned at the far-left side of the display while the inventory and player-model panel remain open.

steps.action: In one continuous horizontal motion, move the mouse cursor from the far-left side across the inventory and player-model area to the far-right side of the full-screen display. Do not click, close the inventory, land, or repeat the trigger before handing off.
steps.success_cue: The cursor has just reached the far-right side after crossing from left to right, and the inventory player-model panel remains open during the Elytra glide.

stor.handoff_condition: The Survival inventory is open while the player remains in an active southward Elytra glide, and the mouse cursor has just been moved once from the far-left side to the far-right side of the full-screen display. Begin observation of the inventory player model immediately, before the player lands or the inventory closes.
uncertainties: The first listed affected version is Minecraft 1.4.2, but the report's current Steps to Reproduce require an Elytra. Elytra were introduced in snapshot 15w41a, so the current Elytra procedure cannot be executed in Minecraft 1.4.2. Minecraft 15w41b is therefore selected as the earliest listed affected version that supports the report's current procedure.

The earliest affected versions correspond to the ticket's historical death/dying inventory reproduction, which the report says ceased to be usable when the inventory began closing on death. This plan intentionally follows only the report's current Elytra reproduction path.

The report does not require a specific game mode, seed, coordinate, altitude, or world type. Starting in Creative mode, ascending to Y=180 or higher, and changing to Survival mode while airborne are practical choices that remove item-acquisition and tower-building randomness without changing the Elytra inventory condition.

Full-screen mode is used because the report explicitly discusses cursor behavior at the left and right sides of a full-screen display, although it also indicates that cursor movement across a windowed Minecraft display may be sufficient.
Southward flight is selected from a report comment describing it as a particularly clear orientation case. The main Steps to Reproduce do not state that southward travel is mandatory.

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition Minecraft 1.7.10 in an unmodified singleplayer world using keyboard and mouse. Use Creative mode with commands enabled only to obtain the setup items, then change the player to Survival mode before placing and targeting the item frame.
preconditions: A Minecraft: Java Edition launcher installation capable of starting the exact profile Minecraft 1.7.10 is available.
Use a singleplayer world; the report does not require a dedicated server, multiple players, a particular seed, or particular coordinates.
Commands must be enabled so the setup can change the player from Creative mode to Survival mode.
The Pick Block control must be bound to an available input. Its default keyboard-and-mouse binding is the middle mouse button, shown as Button 3 in controls.
The player must have at least two item frames before entering Survival mode so that one can be placed while another remains in the inventory.
A non-item-frame item must remain available for selection after the item frame is placed.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that uses the exact version Minecraft 1.7.10, start the game, and wait for the main menu to appear. Do not use a later fix version for this reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is visible and the displayed game version is 1.7.10.

steps.action: From the main menu, open Options, then Controls. Locate the action named Pick Block. Leave it bound to Button 3, the default middle mouse button, or record the alternate bound input if the controls were previously changed. Return to the main menu after checking the binding.
steps.success_cue: The executor knows which physical input activates Pick Block; by default, it is the middle mouse button.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World to open the world-creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Click the Game Mode button until it displays Game Mode: Creative. Creative mode is used only to obtain deterministic setup items without crafting or exploration.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Open More World Options, ensure Allow Cheats is set to ON, return to the main world-creation screen if necessary, and select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: World generation begins with Creative mode and commands enabled.

steps.action: Wait for the world to finish loading. Do not continue until nearby terrain is rendered and movement and inventory input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in the loaded world and is currently in Creative mode.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Identify the hotbar as the row of nine slots at the bottom of the screen; hotbar slot 1 is the leftmost slot and slot 2 is immediately to its right.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open and the nine hotbar slots are visible.

steps.action: Open the Search Items tab, click its search field, and search for Item Frame. Move a stack containing at least two item frames into hotbar slot 1. A larger Creative stack is acceptable, but at least two must be present so one remains after one is placed.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains at least two item frames.

steps.action: Clear or replace the search text, search for Stone, and move a stack containing at least two stone blocks into hotbar slot 2. One stone will provide a support surface, and at least one remaining stone will be the non-item-frame item held during the trigger.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains item frames and hotbar slot 2 contains at least two stone blocks.

steps.action: Press E or Escape to close the inventory and return to first-person world view.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed and the hotbar is visible at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Press 2 to select hotbar slot 2 containing stone. The active hotbar slot is the slot surrounded by the selection outline.
steps.success_cue: Stone is visible in the player's hand and hotbar slot 2 has the active-slot outline.

steps.action: Aim at an open top surface of the ground and press the Use Item/Place Block control once, which is right-click by default, to place one stone block. Choose a position with at least one unobstructed vertical side at player eye level or below.
steps.success_cue: A stone block has been placed with an exposed vertical side, and at least one stone remains in hotbar slot 2.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the exact historical command /gamemode 0, including the leading slash, and press Enter. If the command is rejected because commands are unavailable, stop and recreate or reopen the world with commands enabled before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The command completes and the Survival HUD, including health and hunger indicators, is visible.

steps.action: Press 1 to select hotbar slot 1 containing the item frames.
steps.success_cue: An item frame is visible in the player's hand and hotbar slot 1 has the active-slot outline.

steps.action: Center the crosshair on an exposed vertical side of the placed stone block and press the Use Item control once, which is right-click by default, to place exactly one empty item frame. Do not place an item inside the frame.
steps.success_cue: One empty item frame is attached to the vertical face of the stone block, and at least one item frame remains elsewhere in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Press 2 to switch the active hotbar selection from the item frames to the remaining stone. Confirm that the player is holding stone, not an item frame.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 2 is active, stone is visible in the player's hand, and at least one item frame is still present in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Stand close enough to interact with the placed item frame, approximately two to four blocks away, and move the view until the crosshair is directly over the empty item frame rather than the supporting stone block or surrounding air. Keep the stone selected.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is centered on the item frame entity while Survival mode remains active and stone remains selected.

steps.action: Activate Pick Block exactly once while continuing to look directly at the item frame. With default controls, press the middle mouse button once; if Pick Block was rebound in step 2, press that configured input instead. Do not manually select another hotbar slot after sending the input.
steps.exact_input: Middle mouse button / configured Pick Block input
steps.success_cue: One Pick Block input has just been sent while the crosshair targeted the item frame entity; no further inventory or hotbar input has been made.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in Survival mode, an empty item frame is attached to the stone support, at least one item frame remains in hotbar slot 1, stone was selected in hotbar slot 2, and Pick Block has just been activated once while the crosshair targeted the item frame. Hand off immediately without changing the selected slot or pressing Pick Block again.
uncertainties: The report covers both Survival and Adventure mode, but its concrete reproduction instructions explicitly use Survival mode. This plan therefore uses Survival as the simplest deterministic variant; Adventure can be tested separately if broader mode coverage is required.
The report does not prescribe a seed, coordinates, multiplayer environment, or dedicated server configuration. A default singleplayer world is used as a practical execution choice.

The report does not specify how the item frames should be obtained. Creative inventory is used to avoid crafting and exploration while preserving the required order: obtain the frames, change to Survival, and then place one.

The report asks for two item frames. The Creative inventory may provide a larger stack; this plan treats at least two as sufficient because the reproduction-relevant state is one placed item frame plus at least one matching item frame remaining in inventory.

The report lists 24w44a in both Affects versions and Fix versions. It has been retained in affected_versions because every supplied affected-version entry must be copied exactly, but it is not selected as the recommended reproduction version.
The historical command /gamemode 0 is used for Minecraft 1.7.10 rather than modernizing the procedure to a newer command or game-mode-switching UI.

External verification was limited to operational control and item-frame placement details from permitted Minecraft Wiki sources; the supplied Mojira report remains the primary source of reproduction requirements.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition, exact client version Minecraft 1.4.2, local singleplayer, and two distinct authenticated player profiles with different usernames. Both profiles must launch the game using the same game directory and therefore the same saves folder. Use a fresh Creative-mode world for this minimal two-player-profile reproduction; LAN and a dedicated server are not required for the selected variant.
preconditions: Two distinct Minecraft Java Edition player profiles are available; designate them Player 1 and Player 2.
Player 1 and Player 2 have different usernames. Do not use the same profile under two labels.
Both profiles can launch the exact affected version Minecraft 1.4.2.
Both profiles use the same Minecraft game directory, so a world created by Player 1 remains visible in the Singleplayer world list after switching to Player 2.
Player 2 has never opened the new test world before the trigger step.
Do not use the workaround from the report: do not delete or edit the Data > Player entry in level.dat.
Close the game completely before changing from Player 1 to Player 2; do not leave the world open to LAN or run both clients simultaneously for this variant.

steps.action: Configure or select a launcher installation that starts the exact affected Java Edition version Minecraft 1.4.2. Ensure its game directory will be reused when launching both player profiles.
steps.success_cue: The selected installation identifies its game version as Minecraft 1.4.2 and points to the shared game directory that will contain the test world.

steps.action: Sign in as Player 1 and launch Minecraft 1.4.2. Wait for the main menu to become responsive.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft 1.4.2 is at the main menu under Player 1's distinct account identity.

steps.action: Open the local world menu by clicking Singleplayer, then click Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Enter the world name MC-697-Repro. Click the Game Mode button until it displays Creative, then click Create New World. Do not configure a special seed; the bug does not depend on terrain generation.
steps.exact_input: World Name: MC-697-Repro; Game Mode: Creative
steps.success_cue: The world named MC-697-Repro begins loading in Creative mode.

steps.action: Wait for world creation and terrain loading to finish. Do not continue while the loading screen is visible or while nearby terrain is still failing to render.
steps.success_cue: Player 1 can see rendered terrain, look around, and move normally in the newly created world.

steps.action: Press E, using the default Inventory control, to open Player 1's Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory item grid and the player's hotbar slots are visible.

steps.action: Locate the Block of Diamond in the Creative inventory and place a stack into hotbar slot 1. Locate the Block of Gold and place a stack into hotbar slot 2. Use left-click to pick up each item stack and left-click the intended hotbar slot to place it. These items are a distinctive Player 1 inventory marker; no crafting is required.
steps.exact_input: Block of Diamond -> hotbar slot 1; Block of Gold -> hotbar slot 2
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains Block of Diamond items and hotbar slot 2 contains Block of Gold items.

steps.action: Press E to close the inventory. Press the number key 1 to make hotbar slot 1 the active slot.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed, hotbar slot 1 is highlighted, and Player 1 visibly holds a Block of Diamond.

steps.action: Leave Player 1 in the world briefly without dropping or placing the two inventory marker stacks. This establishes a nonempty, readily identifiable player state for the world save.
steps.success_cue: Player 1 remains in the loaded world with Block of Diamond in slot 1, Block of Gold in slot 2, and slot 1 selected.

steps.action: Press Esc to open the pause menu, then click Save and Quit to Title. Wait until the main menu is fully displayed. This saves Player 1's current state as the world's singleplayer/default player data.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The main menu is displayed and MC-697-Repro is no longer open.

steps.action: Exit Minecraft completely rather than only returning to the main menu. Wait until the game process has closed.
steps.success_cue: No Minecraft 1.4.2 game window remains open and the launcher can change accounts safely.

steps.action: In the launcher, sign out of Player 1 or change the active account, then sign in as the distinct Player 2 profile. Do not move, copy, convert, or edit the MC-697-Repro world.
steps.success_cue: The launcher is authenticated as Player 2, whose username differs from Player 1's username.

steps.action: Using the same installation and shared game directory from step 1, launch Minecraft 1.4.2 as Player 2. Wait for the main menu to become responsive.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft 1.4.2 is at the main menu under Player 2's account identity.

steps.action: Click Singleplayer and locate the existing world named MC-697-Repro. Do not create a second world and do not use Open to LAN.
steps.success_cue: MC-697-Repro appears in Player 2's Singleplayer world list, confirming that both profiles are accessing the same saved world folder.

steps.action: Select MC-697-Repro and click Play Selected World, or double-click the world entry once. This world-opening action is the reproduction trigger.
steps.success_cue: The world loading screen appears for the existing MC-697-Repro world under Player 2's profile.

steps.action: Wait until the world has finished loading. Do not open the inventory, change hotbar selection, move items, issue commands, or save and quit before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: Player 2 is in the loaded MC-697-Repro world, surrounding terrain is rendered, and normal camera or movement input responds; Player 2's inventory and position have not yet been altered after loading.

stor.handoff_condition: Player 2 has just opened the existing MC-697-Repro singleplayer world originally created and saved by Player 1. Terrain loading has completed, input is responsive, and Player 2 has not yet moved items, changed the selected hotbar slot, opened a container, or saved the world. Begin observing the loaded player state now.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a formal numbered Steps to Reproduce section. This plan reconstructs the minimum same-computer, two-account path from the description and supporting comments.

The report describes three related situations: a different player opening another player's world, an existing LAN participant playerdata entry being ignored, and default data becoming outdated after dedicated-server play. This plan intentionally selects only the simplest first situation; it does not establish the LAN or dedicated-server variants.

No game mode, seed, world name, inventory contents, or location is prescribed by the report. A fresh Creative world and distinctive diamond/gold block inventory markers are practical execution choices, not asserted bug requirements.

The exact arrangement of the Minecraft 1.4.2 Creative inventory depends on the historical UI and selected language. If the named blocks are not immediately visible, locate them by their item names or icons without substituting items unavailable in Minecraft 1.4.2.

The plan assumes the launcher permits both profiles to use one shared game directory. If account-specific installations use different game directories, the same unmodified MC-697-Repro world folder must be made accessible to Player 2 before step 14 without opening or converting it in another version.
